topic: The bullet train that copied a bird

lines.say: Four hundred metres from a tunnel, homes heard Japan's bullet train boom.
Its blunt nose squeezed the air inside the tunnel.
That squeeze raced ahead at the speed of sound
and burst from the exit. Boom.
Engineer Eiji Nakatsu, a birdwatcher, thought of the kingfisher,
which dives from air into water with barely a splash.
So the five hundred Series got a fifteen-metre beak for a nose.
Now the air is squeezed gently. The boom fades.
Ten percent faster, on fifteen percent less power.
Follow for how the world is really engineered.
